title: What amateur radio is for
blurb: The big idea before the cards.

lines.caption: Amateur radio is a licensed service. Part of its purpose is to grow your skill at building radios and at using them.
lines.label: why it exists

lines.caption: One agency writes and enforces the rules: the FCC, the Federal Communications Commission.
lines.say: One agency writes and enforces the rules: the F C C, the Federal Communications Commission.
lines.label: the rule maker

lines.caption: Your license is real once it shows up in the FCC's online license database, the ULS.
lines.say: Your license is real once it shows up in the F C C's online license database, the U L S.
lines.label: proof of your license

lines.caption: Hams share the air. Local volunteers recommend repeater channels, and nobody may interfere on purpose.
lines.label: sharing the air

lines.caption: Some stations are special. A ham station more than fifty kilometers up is a space station.
lines.label: more than 50 km up

lines.caption: Now meet each rule in a small situation.
